title: 1.1  The cities are rebuilt, the mods are on Nexus as a collection, and everyone starts over
details: THE COLLECTION. Thornswood's mod list is published on Nexus now, as a collection Vortex installs for you. That means every mod comes from its own author rather than from a copy of ours, a mod update stops meaning a reinstall, and the day the installer drops the mods it goes from fourteen gigabytes to a fraction of that.
The launcher has a card at the top of the Add-ons tab with the link, and a Help section on Vortex profiles: making one, switching between them, and how to put your own Skyrim back when you are done.

The installer does not carry the mods any more. It is the launcher and Thornswood's own content, which is why it went from fourteen gigabytes to under one. The collection is where the mods come from now, so following it is not optional: without it you have a launcher, no mods, and the server turns you away when you press Play. The launcher sends you to it.
If the wrong profile is active in Vortex, the launcher says so before you press Play, instead of letting you load into what looks like plain Skyrim and then getting turned away by the server.

YOUR CHARACTERS HAVE BEEN WIPED. Taking a plugin out of the middle of the load order moves every plugin below it, and the game works out what an item is by counting positions. Characters made under the old numbering would have ended up holding the wrong things. Everyone starts again. This is the last time it happens before launch.
THE CITIES.
JK's Skyrim is in, the all in one version, which overhauls the clutter, signage and layout of every city and town.

JK's Whiterun and JK's Riverwood are out. They were the older standalone versions of the same work. Comparing them record by record, every one of JK's Whiterun's 155 edits is also in the all in one, and 138 of JK's Riverwood's 143. Keeping both would have meant one silently overwriting the other.

The Great Cities, Minor Cities and Towns is out. It and JK's Skyrim edit 413 of the same records, 82 of them navmeshes, and navmesh conflicts are what make guards walk into walls. The patch that fixes it needs the whole Cities of the North set, and two of those need Creation Club content we cannot ship. It was one or the other.
Capital Windhelm keeps its own patch, CWE - JK - United, which resolves the 124 records it shares with JK's.
Riften Expansion is in, along with its JK's Skyrim patch.
JK's Castle Volkihar, JK's Markarth Outskirts and JK's Riften Outskirts are in. Those are the separate Outskirts series and they sit alongside the all in one rather than on top of it.
MODS ADDED
SkyHUD, the interface overhaul.
Tavern Games, mini games in inns.
New Legion, Imperial armour replacer, with its textures.
Respawn, which changes what happens when you die.
Carriage and Ferry Travel Overhaul, carriage and ferry routes between holds.
Skyrim Unbound Reborn, the alternate start, with its Orc Strongholds, Thalmor, Blackreach Laboratory and Meeko's Shack additions and its patches for Guard Dialogue Overhaul and Capital Windhelm.
Playable Lute, Flute and Drum, which the bard emotes use.
JK's Skyrim, all in one.
JK's Castle Volkihar, JK's Markarth Outskirts and JK's Riften Outskirts.
CWE - JK - United, the Capital Windhelm patch.
Riften Expansion, and its JK's Skyrim patch.
Thornswood's own content plugin, which was always there and is now installed properly alongside the rest.
MODS REMOVED
Missives, the notice board quests. We are building our own notice boards, so it was doing a job twice.
JK's Whiterun and JK's Riverwood, both superseded by JK's Skyrim all in one.
The Great Cities, Minor Cities and Towns, which cannot coexist with JK's Skyrim without a patch that is not available to us.

Two plugins that were quietly broken have been switched off. GourmetFishing needed a Creation Club file that is not in the build, and the Riften Expansion patch for JK's Skyrim needed a mod that was not in the profile. That second one is back on now that JK's Skyrim is.

The load order is 96 plugins, and the collection installs every one of them. It did not before: the script extender framework was missing from it entirely, and three plugins the server checks for were loose files that only existed on one machine.
LAUNCHER
Add-ons tab, with optional packs you can install and remove one at a time.
Delete buttons next to your own files and next to script extender plugins, so leaving Thornswood does not have to mean throwing away mods you still want for somewhere else.
Uninstall now asks whether to delete the mods. Leave the box unticked and they stay, so reinstalling later costs you minutes instead of an evening.
The Fix button greys itself out when it cannot help. It repairs the plugin list, it cannot install a missing mod, and it used to let you press it anyway.
A new Help section on Vortex profiles: making one, switching between them, and how to put your own Skyrim back to normal when you are done.
Signing in with Discord now returns you to the panel instead of leaving you looking at a browser tab.
Field of view is adjustable, from 60 to 140.
ACCESS

The door is connected. The game server now pulls the allowed list from the site every five minutes, and the site builds that list from Discord roles, so Playtester and staff are on it and nobody else is. It is watching rather than turning people away while the list fills up, because enforcing it the day it goes in would turn away everybody who has not pressed Play since the launcher started sending their profile id. Once the log shows the right names it starts biting.
PROFESSIONS

The Professions and classes page now has the mage plan written out. Two schools and two starting spells, and you can hold the spells back instead, so the slots stay open for something further up that you would rather have. Rank opens higher spells and more spell slots at the same time, and at Master a mage picks a third school.

Anybody who did not take Mage can still learn magic. It takes the book and a Master rank mage willing to apprentice them, and there is a cap on how many spells anyone picks up that way, so it stays something you know rather than a mage with extra steps.

A Master in any profession can take an apprentice, and it has to be somebody in the same profession and the same half of it. An armour smith teaches armour smiths. While it stands the apprentice climbs faster, so hours spent under somebody who already got there are worth more than the same hours spent alone. The master decides who, and can end it.

The roadmap has been brought up to date. Everything this release shipped moved into Done, the professions line now says what is actually left of it, and the gallery and the optional looks came off the list of things still to build, because they are built.
DISCORD

The ticket panel has an Apply: Jarl option. It is answered in character, and the first people to hold a seat are picked out of what gets written there. It asks which hold, who the character is, what their claim is, what changes under them, and what happens the day somebody takes it off them.

The ticket panel updates itself now. A new kind added to the list used to exist in the bot and never appear in the channel, because the options a dropdown offers live in the posted message rather than in the code.
FIXES
The launcher used to keep running invisibly after you closed it, so it refused to open again until you killed it by hand.
The welcome card in Discord fires on join again.

The release history on the website went empty a second time, for a different reason than the first. PowerShell hands a one item list back out of a function as a bare string, so every entry that had a single line of detail was published as text rather than a list. The page threw the moment it reached one and reported it as the whole page failing to load. Fixed in the publisher, in what the site hands out, and in the page that reads it, so no one of the three can do it alone again.

title: Add-ons tab, optional packs, Discord sign in returns to the panel
details: The launcher has an Add-ons tab. Textures, weather and shaders go on and come off one at a time, they are yours alone, and nobody else has to download any of it to play with you.
It also carries the card with the collection link, and a Help section on Vortex profiles: making one, switching between them, and putting your own Skyrim back the way it was when you are done.
Signing in with Discord leaves you looking at the launcher rather than at a browser tab it opened and forgot about.
There are delete buttons next to your own files and next to script extender plugins, so leaving Thornswood does not mean throwing away mods you still want somewhere else.

title: Professions, sub professions and classes at character creation
details: Character creation asks for all three now. A profession, which half of it you do, and a class, which is where your raw material comes from.
Skyrim's own levelling is switched off. Nothing you do raises a vanilla skill and no perk menu opens when you sleep, so nothing anybody does today is being spent on a system that is going away.
Nobody gets all three sides of anything, which is the point. A smith who cannot mine needs a miner, and a miner with no smith has a bag of ore.
What each half can actually make, and the four ranks it opens as you climb them, are still being built. The whole plan is written out on the Professions and classes page.

title: Connect your Discord from the launcher
details: One click in the launcher. Your browser opens, you say yes, it closes itself, and you never do it again.

That is what ties your Discord account to the character you play as, which is what the door on the server reads. One list decides who is allowed in the game, the site and the chat, so losing the role in Discord stops the next launch with nothing to remember to change anywhere else.

title: The launcher reopens, and you can set your field of view
details: Closing the launcher used to leave it running where you could not see it, so it refused to open again until you killed it by hand.
Field of view is in the launcher now, anywhere from 60 to 140.

title: Skyrim has people in it again
details: The server was turning away every playable race, which is why the world was empty. It is not any more.

title: Your armour stays on and your spells stay in your hand
details: Looting a body used to strip whatever you were wearing off you.
Spells from mods were being taken back out of your hands the moment you equipped them.

title: Doors and chests are locked again
details: Every lock in Skyrim was open. All of them.
Handles, chains and cage gates activate properly now too.

title: Enemies have their own health
details: Everything you fought was reporting your health instead of its own, so nothing ever died when it should have.
Enchantment hits count as damage now as well.

title: Voice moved into the launcher
details: It used to run inside the game and lose the microphone.
Whisper and yell change how far you carry, and the indicator now tells you the truth about whether you are heard.

title: You get a warning before the server goes down
details: A countdown in the world, then back to the launcher, instead of being dropped mid sentence.

title: Guards stop hunting you after you die
details: The resisted arrest flag was never clearing, so the whole hold stayed angry with you forever.

title: The keyboard stays with the game
details: Voice opening used to steal your keys, which meant you could hear everyone and move nowhere.

title: Your inventory saves
details: What you were carrying is on the server now, so it is still there next time.

title: Bards can play, and voice is ready in seconds
details: Instruments work.
Voice used to take the best part of twenty seconds after loading in. It takes two.
